extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, math-education reform practitioners, university administrators, and researchers studying departmental change
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and descriptive criteria for judging how well university mathematics departments adopt, support, and institutionalize mathematics education reform (MER), based on survey data and case studies. Includes indicators of departmental attitudes, faculty involvement, curricular changes, institutional support, and network/organizational practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary indicators of positive departmental attitude changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary indicators of positive departmental attitude changes toward mathematics education reform are: (1) improvements in curricula, (2) new institutional support and (3) attention to better pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of curricular improvements include adoption of reform calculus programs (e.g., Harvard calculus), development of entry-level and graduate courses on pedagogy, remedial education reform, re-writing pre-service programs, emerging scholars programs, and designing math/science cores. Institutional support can be manifested as funding, workshops, or administrative backing; attention to pedagogy shows up as seminars, colloquia, and departmental discussion of teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental valuation and acceptance of education reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey items: 'Involvement in mathematics education reform is highly valued in my department' and 'In my department, the atmosphere toward mathematics education reform is one of acceptance and support.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these items to assess departmental attitude: distinctions matter between 'accepted' and 'highly valued' — many departments may accept education work but not value it as highly as research. Both acceptance and high valuation are meaningful signals for reform sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent departmental support for new projects/programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item: 'During the past five years, new projects and programs related to mathematics education have been supported by my department.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count and characterize supported initiatives (e.g., workshops hosted, curricular revisions, grant activity). High percentages of support over a recent timeframe indicate momentum; consider external policy pressures when attributing causation to MER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty participation levels in educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in various activities (K-12 reform, undergraduate reform, teacher preparation, graduate reform for math students, graduate reform for math-education students, teacher in-service, mathematics research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey reports show relatively few faculty involved in most educational initiatives (often <20%); undergraduate reform for majors typically has the highest involvement. Use percent engaged across categories to gauge breadth and depth of departmental engagement; sustained reform requires broader faculty participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reward structures for education work
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators of institutional support such as consideration in promotion and tenure decisions, release time for educational involvement, administrative respect, and hiring/promotion for education work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether educational activities are rewarded (tenure/promotion credit, release time), and look for concrete examples (faculty promoted for national educational efforts, hiring for education roles). Changing reward structures is necessary for sustained reform beyond individual efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of faculty time use with departmental expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of actual time respondents spend (hours per week; percent time on teaching, research, education reform, service, administration) versus their perceptions of departmental expectations for promotion and tenure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies (e.g., faculty spending more time on education than departments expect) signal potential misalignment that can hinder reform. Use mean hours and percent-time distributions to assess workload and perceived institutional priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimization of mathematics education within research community
rubrics_metrics.description: MER's role in legitimizing mathematics education reform and reducing its 'second-class' status among mathematicians ('Affecting positively mathematics education reform mainly by legitimizing mathematics education and get rid of its second-class status').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess changes in perceived respectability, willingness of mathematicians to engage publicly in education work, and whether participants feel empowered to push for changes on campus as measures of legitimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental culture promoting ongoing study of educational responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Model departments are those 'in which the departmental culture promotes regular, thoughtful study of its educational responsibilities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for institutionalized practices such as regular seminars, faculty development time, workshops, newsletters, and structured interdepartmental communication that indicate a culture of continual attention to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad-based faculty participation vs. isolated individual projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainable reform requires educational goals to be 'integral to the departmental mission and are supported by broadly based faculty participation' rather than projects seen as 'Professor X's project' dependent on a founder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether reform activities are distributed across faculty ranks and roles and whether an 'overall vision' and 'unified purpose' exist. Identify reliance on adjunct/untenured faculty versus tenure-track commitment to judge institutionalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental mission balance (research, teaching, service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments typically balance research, teaching, and service; at research-oriented institutions research and teaching are highest priority while service to the non-university community is least.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how departmental mission priorities affect willingness to adopt education reforms (e.g., heavy emphasis on research may limit support for education unless teaching/reform are valued in promotion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting research-oriented departments for leverage
rubrics_metrics.description: MER focuses on research-oriented mathematics departments because they influence other post-secondary institutions and are key to changing undergraduate and graduate mathematics education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scaling reform, prioritize departments with research prestige or influence. Evaluate impact on broader systems when these departments adopt reform practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network practices for departmental change
rubrics_metrics.description: Departmental network design features: three-year experiment, teams of 3-5 faculty sent to workshops, sharing experiences among departments, and focusing on developing models of departments where education goals are integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these procedural elements as criteria for program design and evaluation: team-based participation, multi-year commitment, interdepartmental exchange, and emphasis on creating transferable departmental models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and recruitment as part of reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic indicators: representation of women and minorities among faculty and graduate students, and departmental strategies to recruit and retain underrepresented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate recruitment strategies, retention rates, and graduate program demographics as components of reform aimed at broadening participation; low faculty diversity may impede inclusive reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete signs of departmental educational activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Observable activities such as seminars on teaching and learning, email newsletters, hosting MER workshops, experimental/innovative teaching approaches, and involvement in teacher preparation and in-service projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog and weigh these concrete activities when judging departmental engagement: frequency, attendance, institutionalization, and whether they lead to curriculum or policy change.
